title: Review: Kinematics
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Physics (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-29-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: A.1#c06 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; A.1#c13 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; A.1#c08 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; A.1#c15 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: A.1#q01, A.1#q02, A.1#q22, A.1#q05, A.1#q07, A.1#q09, A.1#q21, A.1#q03, A.1#q04, A.1#q23, A.1#q06, A.1#q08. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: The total length of the path travelled by a body.

items.label: Uniform acceleration
items.clue: Velocity changes by equal amounts in equal times.

items.label: Average velocity
items.clue: The displacement divided by the time interval over which it occurs, Δx/Δt.

items.label: Acceleration of free fall, g
items.clue: The acceleration of a body moving under gravity alone, with no fluid resistance.

questions.stem: A body moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the body?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.

questions.explanation: The negative velocity means the body is moving left. The acceleration points the opposite way, so the speed decreases: after 1.5 s the velocity is zero. The acceleration is still +2.0 m s⁻² at that instant, so the velocity then becomes positive and the body moves right, speeding up.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Fluid resistance is negligible and upwards is taken as positive. Which statement about the ball at the instant it reaches its highest point is correct?

options.text: Its velocity is zero, so its acceleration is zero as well.
Its acceleration is reversing from upwards to downwards.
Its acceleration is changing sign from negative to positive.
Its velocity is zero; its acceleration is g downwards.

questions.explanation: At the top the velocity changes from positive to negative, so it is momentarily zero. It is still changing at that instant, so the acceleration is not zero: it is g downwards (−g), as at every other point of the flight.

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Observer A measures her position from a marker M, taking the direction in which she first runs as positive. Observer B measures her position from a marker N, which is 15 m from M in the positive direction, and takes the same direction as positive. According to observer A, the runner starts at +25 m, runs to +95 m, turns round, runs back to +5.0 m and stops. What is the displacement of the runner according to observer B?
A body moves from point P to point Q. Which statement about its displacement is correct?

options.text: Its magnitude can be less than the distance travelled, but never greater.
It equals the total length of the path followed from P to Q.
It depends on the route taken, whereas the distance does not.
It is always positive, because it is a length measured in metres.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line change in position from P to Q; distance is the length of the path. The straight line is the shortest route, so the magnitude of the displacement equals the distance only for one-way motion along a straight line and is otherwise smaller.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest at t = 0 and x = 0 and moves along a straight road. A graph of its position x against time t is a curve that gets steeper with time. At t = 3.0 s, x = 16.5 m, and the tangent to the curve at this point also passes through the point (5.0 s, 40.5 m). What is the instantaneous velocity of the car at t = 3.0 s?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the gradient of the tangent to the position–time graph: (40.5 − 16.5) m ÷ (5.0 − 3.0) s = 24 m ÷ 2.0 s = 12 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A stone is released from rest and falls 5.00 m. Fluid resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the stone when it has fallen 5.00 m?
questions.explanation: With downwards positive, v² = u² + 2as = 0 + 2 × 9.8 × 5.00 = 98.0 m² s⁻², so v = √98.0 = 9.90 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: The position x of a body moving along a straight line is recorded at intervals of 1.0 s, starting at t = 0: x = 0, 5.0 m, 8.0 m, 9.0 m, 8.0 m, 5.0 m and 0. Which statement about the motion of the body is correct?

options.text: The acceleration is zero at t = 3.0 s, because the body is momentarily at rest at that time.
The acceleration is negative up to t = 3.0 s, then positive as the body speeds up again.
The acceleration is constant and negative; the body reverses direction at t = 3.0 s.
The acceleration decreases while the body slows down, then increases as it speeds up.

questions.stem: A graph of velocity against time for a trolley moving along a straight track is a straight line from (0 s, 1.0 m s⁻¹) to (2.0 s, 4.0 m s⁻¹). What is the acceleration of the trolley at t = 2.0 s?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, the gradient of the velocity–time graph. The line is straight, so the gradient is the same at every instant: (4.0 − 1.0) m s⁻¹ ÷ 2.0 s = 1.5 m s⁻².

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns round and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?
questions.explanation: Displacement is the change in position: x(final) − x(initial) = (−20 m) − (+30 m) = −50 m. The turning point at +70 m affects the distance travelled but not the displacement.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from a point 1.20 m above the ground. It rises to a maximum height of 6.70 m above the ground, falls, and is caught at a point 1.70 m above the ground. Upwards is taken as positive. What are the distance travelled by the ball and its displacement, from the throw to the catch?
questions.explanation: Distance is the length of the path: 5.50 m up then 5.00 m down, 10.5 m in total. Displacement is the change in position, final minus initial: 1.70 m − 1.20 m = +0.50 m, upwards.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: The outward leg takes 300 s and the return leg 200 s, so average speed = 6000 m ÷ 500 s = 12 m s⁻¹. The car finishes where it started, so its displacement is zero and so is its average velocity.

questions.stem: A car travelling at 16 m s⁻¹ brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in 4.0 s. What distance does the car travel while braking?
questions.explanation: With uniform acceleration, s = ((u + v)/2)t = ((16 + 0)/2) × 4.0 = 32 m. The same answer follows from s = ut + ½at² with a = −4.0 m s⁻²: 64 − 32 = 32 m.
